status: fixed before localization experiment; exploratory mechanism diagnosis, not a new performance benchmark
scope: Localize remaining CPU gradient discrepancies while retaining previous failed FP32 gate results
source: Same six saved TensorFlow fixtures and original float32 weights; hashes must match export.json
precision_conditions: same input values and realized float32 weights promoted to float64, no new initialization
measurements: Replay original TensorFlow and PyTorch losses and all parameter gradients; preserve unchanged parity rule
Separate gradients by each input row, each contribution scaled by 1/3 to reconstruct the original batch mean
For Conv5 and Conv7 export actual post-ReLU tensors and loss cotangents
Compare ReLU masks and predict the isolated mask-change contribution to bias gradients
Reconstruct bias gradients from identical cotangents using float64 summation
Apply original TensorFlow BiasAdd gradient and PyTorch bias-add gradient to identical fixed cotangents, isolating reduction from the rest of the network
Compare corrected candidate across frameworks in float64 as a localization control only
interpretation_rules: A float64 diagnostic pass does not erase or pass the historical float32 gate
A discrepancy reproduced with identical cotangents localizes a reduction difference independently of the learned model
A difference predicted by ReLU mask changes is distinguished from a bias reduction discrepancy
A remaining discrepancy without a measured mechanism stays unresolved; no cause is assumed
No clipping, tolerance relaxation, per-seed backend selection, training data or model-architecture change
This mechanism study does not establish the cause of the full-training collapse
